utterances.text: You've described one occasion when Arkan showed up at this facility and your brother refused to allow him to enter. And this was at transcript page 19367 through -69. Did Arkan announce himself when he came up to the gate?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he introduced himself right away. Or maybe several minutes later. I wasn't present at the moment he arrived. However, a few minutes following the alarm signal, when assistance was needed, I arrived at the gate and my late brother told me that it was Arkan. I don't know if he introduced himself to my brother as Arkan or whether he used his first and last name. At the moment of my arrival, which was, say, after three to five minutes, they were there. I wasn't there from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: How were -- how was Arkan dressed; and how were his seven or eight escorts dressed?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all in uniform. Camouflage military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And they were armed; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: When you were asked why Arkan wanted to enter Pajzos, you told us that: "... well, I suppose he may have wanted to take the wine away or perhaps to see whether there was any wine there. So that must have been the reason why he was shouting. He also mentioned the wine. And he even said, What? I want to buy some wine." Is it your evidence that the only reason Arkan showed up at this Serbian DB reconnaissance outpost with seven or eight escorts in combat uniforms and with weapons was to buy wine?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only reason I could hear mentioned when I arrived, since I can't talk about what happened before, is what I was told by my late brother. As of the moment of my arrival, the only reason he mentioned that I could hear for him wishing to enter was wine. There was plenty of wine in the cellars. Perhaps he wanted it. I really can't say. As far as I could hear, the only reason he gave was the wine. He said, So what? Perhaps I want to buy some wine. Perhaps he was mocking us, but that was the only thing he mentioned as of the moment of my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Jordash, do you have any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- in re-direct? Go ahead, please. Further cross-examination by Mr. Jordash:

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. You've been asked many questions about documents which are alleged to come from DB archives. I just want to clarify what you know and what you don't know about DB archives. Do you know who was in charge of those DB archives? If, indeed, they were DB archives.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It would be a secret anyhow, so I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Do you know who would have access to those DB archives at any time between 1991 and 1998?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: So you wouldn't know who, if so minded, could have put documents in those archives for reasons less to do with truth and more to do with benefits, such as pensions and so on?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Are you able to comment on whether -- do you know anything about pensions and benefits, such as pensions which DB -- those engaged by the DB might be entitled to? Do you know anything about them?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Are you able to say this: That benefits and pensions within the DB and within the Serbian MUP were connected to length of service for the DB? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know who was supposed to decide who deserved a pension or benefit and what it all depended on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: So you're not able to confirm that pensions, for example, were connected to those who'd served for a particular number of years? You couldn't get a pension unless you'd served for a number of years. Are you able to say anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment. It strikes me as logical that I would need to serve a certain number of years in order to be entitled to a pension, such as in my case, for example.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Do you have a pension? Or did you receive a pension from the DB, or other such benefits?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only received regular salaries. And not from the State Security Service but from the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you didn't receive a pension?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still need a few years of service.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move to another subject. I want to take you to 1992 and 1993 and the issue of paramilitary units or, rather, units which were formed and sometimes were within the VRS command structure and sometimes were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we please have on the screen P3119. Actually, Your Honour, I'm going to try to save time. And if I can save this exhibit for the witness to look at during the break, and the same with another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And I'll take you, instead, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, 65 ter 3821.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a document which we obtained from the Prosecution. And it appears to emanate from the Command of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, Bratunac. And it appears to give a history of the Red Berets from Bratunac. Take a moment to read it, please.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Now, without stating the obvious, the 3rd Infantry Battalion and the Light Infantry Brigade, who were supposed to be the -- those who received this document, were part of the VRS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And are you able to confirm, as we can see from the document, that the Panther Guard was also part of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And, in fact, would you agree with me that the other identified units within this document, whether the Guards unit from Han Pijesak or the Drina Wolves, were all part of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These units were in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Had you heard of the Red Berets from Bratunac, or did you hear about them during the time that you were on the border, or subsequently, as a group which were commanded by, subordinated to, the VRS or Republika Srpska police, as this document seems to indicate?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about these units, although I don't remember when precisely, as it was some 20 years ago. I no longer remember the date on which I heard of the Red Berets from Bratunac, the Panthers, the Wolves from the Drina. But all these are Bosnian units that I heard about in Bajina Basta, perhaps at the watch-tower or shortly afterwards. It was during that period of time in any case. I lived in Bajina Basta, and there were many people coming from Bosnia telling all sorts of things. As part of that, I heard about these units from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, on the screen 1D2238.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: As you can see: Republika Srpska, special brigade -- special police brigade in Bijeljina, 5th of April, 1995, to the RS minister of the interior. Request for payment of funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we go over the page in the English, please, so that -- and also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: We can see a list of soldiers of the Red Berets with the unit commander: Rade, son of Sreten Petrovic. And if we go to the third page of the English, we can see the names there. And if we go to the fourth page of the English and the next page of the B/C/S, we'll also see a list of those who were killed, including Bosko, son of Nedjeljko Neskovic. Is this consistent with your knowledge that the Red Berets -- or do you know anything about this? - the Red Berets, even in April of 1995, being subordinated to Republika Srpska units? This -- on this -- at this point in time, the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that the Red Berets from Bratunac were subordinated to the Republika Srpska. I don't know to which unit exactly. But I know that they were from Republika Srpska and they were either subordinated to the military or to the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. I don't know if you're aware of the - excuse my pronunciation - Blagojevic Judgement in this -- from the -- from this Court, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, at paragraph 56 of the Judgement.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: -- found that in 1995 the Red Berets were under the command of Colonel Blagojevic, commander of the Bratunac Brigade. Had you heard that the Red Berets in 1995 were under the command of Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Fair enough. Just so you're clear what our case is, so I'm not misleading you: I'm not suggesting that no one from the Red Berets under the VRS had contact with anyone -- let me clarify that. I'm not suggesting that there weren't individuals from the Serbian DB who had contact with the Red Berets from Bratunac, but it's our case that the Red Berets from Bratunac were essentially a VRS unit. You follow me?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I note the time, Your Honour. I do apologise. I think I've gone over the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will take a break, and we shall resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just hereby put on the record that we're not -- that my colleagues are not any longer sitting Rule 15 bis. At the same time, I would also like to announce, since I have been unable to read the transcript yet, that Judge Picard acts as Presiding Judge and -- until the next witness appears. So I leave the conduct of the proceedings in her hands, including all matters that arise out of the testimony of this witness. Judge Picard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Jordash, you may proceed. And please tell us, before that, how much more time do you need approximately? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I've been discussing with Mr. Bakrac and in order to try and get the witness finished I'm going to need, I think, 20 minutes. And I think that suits Mr. Bakrac. Whether it suits the overall plan, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You may proceed. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to save time, what I'd like to do is, first of all, to tender the two documents which I've just been asking the witness about. 65 ter 3821, 1D2238. And what I'd also like to do to save time is to tender from the bar table similar documents. And if I can just explain that very briefly. The first two documents, as Your Honour know, were documents which we say demonstrates that the Red Berets from Bratunac were subordinated to either the VRS or Republika Srpska. And then the documents I'd like to bar table are: 1D2002, which is a report on combat readiness in the Bratunac Brigade dated the 26th of September, 1994, which has listed on the third page the Red Berets platoon; 1D107 regular combat report of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, which, again, has the Red Berets listed as a platoon; 2D132, 24th of December, 1994, regular combat report of the Light Infantry Brigade, again, Red Berets platoon, spoken in terms of being part of that brigade. And, finally -- no, that's it. That's what we'd like to do, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Harbour, do you have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We haven't been able to review these documents or verify that we have origin information yet, so if we could have the opportunity to do that before giving our response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this for all documents or just the first two documents that we have looked at? Or can the first two documents be admitted now?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you for asking further clarification. We have no objection to the two documents that were put to the witness being admitted. We've verified their origin information. As for the rest that are being tendered via the bar table, we would like an opportunity to look into them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I imagine that Mr. Simatovic has no objection. Doesn't seem like so. Mr. Registrar, can you please give us the numbers for the first two documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 3821 will be Exhibit D866. And 65 ter number 1D2238 will be Exhibit D867.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. D866 and D867 will be admitted. As for the other documents, it is maybe better to wait for the Prosecutor to be able to consult them. Would you like to have these documents MFI'd for the time being?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, can you please MFI these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 1D2002 will be Exhibit D868 marked for identification; 1D107 will be Exhibit D869, marked for identification; and 2D132 will be Exhibit D870, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much -- [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: -- Mr. Jordash, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Overlapping speakers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Please could we have on the screen 1D1439.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the border and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I think it's 1D1459 that I want. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the border because I'm interested in trying to work out what you know about the way in which these paramilitary groups that we're hearing about, including the Red Berets from Bratunac, how they obtained their logistics and weapons and so on. Would you agree with me -- while that document's being found, would you agree with me that the crossings at Bajina Basta were carefully manned to prevent weapons being taken from Serbia into Bosnia in the time that you were there on the border? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the border, our main duty was to guard the border, ensure that there weren't any crossings from Serbia into Bosnia and from Bosnia into Serbia. As for the border pass at Skelani, it was under the control of the police that performed the same duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Now, this is a State Security Department report from Nis. And I just want to -- and dated the 30th of March, 1993. And if we can go to the second page, this concerns volunteers crossing into Bosnia. And it says on the second page of the English and the B/C/S: "During their departure from Nis on the 26th of March, 1993, the group of volunteers was not carrying fire-arms, as Petrovic had warned them about possible checks in the train and at the border ... in Bajina Basta." Would you agree with me, Mr. Witness, that this description is consistent with what you were doing and what others were doing, i.e., preventing men from entering Bosnia carrying weapons or ammunition and the like, in 1993 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, could we have on the screen, P3119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jordash, I'm interrupting you to tell you the following. The documents that you wanted to be admitted through a bar table motion are not there. There's one testimony; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. They're all reports from the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would seem that that's not the case though. So do we have 1D107; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar will verify. Can you please check, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. You gave us the right number, so you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Let me take you, please, to P3119. Because what I suggest is that rather than weapons being taken into Bosnia to supply paramilitaries in 1992 and 1993, Bosnia itself was awash with weapons, and paramilitaries obtained their weapons locally. Are you able to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, there were a lot of weapons in Bosnia. And according to the information we had, practically everyone was armed there. So there would not really be any need to transfer weapons across, and I'm not aware of that having been done, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Let me take -- this is a report of the Independent Battalion, Skelani, February 1993, as we can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let's go to page 3 of the English, and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And it says there, two-thirds of the way down the page: "Very little attention was devoted to war booty. No records of war booty were kept, and tons of goods were ferried across the Drina river, such as tractors, automobiles, farm machines, livestock," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then over the page to page 4 of the English and 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Situation from 1st of January to 25th of February, 1993. And the paragraph which begins "After the attack by Muslim forces on the 16th of January, 1993," and further down the page, where it says: "When the evacuation began, stories and rumours spread about the VRS General Staff and Republika Srpska Presidency to the effect that someone had sold out this territory, which was followed by a mass laying down of weapons and crossings over into the FRY." Are you able to confirm these remarks, that, first of all, equipment was being ferried into Serbia, personal belongings, war booty, whether belonging to the person carrying it or not, and, secondly, this mass laying down of weapons in the area covered by the Skelani Independent Battalion Brigade -- sorry Skelani Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the 16th of January, people fled from Bosnia en masse. That's well-known. As for this war plan, I don't know what the plan could be, because people were taking their personal belongings with them. In fact, that's what they claimed. They said that the belongs were theirs. But as for weapons, the weapons weren't taken over the bridge. That was prohibited. We didn't have any incidents on the border with Bosnia, so these crossings referred to here took place at the bridge that was under the MUP control. So I do know that no one could take weapons across the territory of Serbia. As for war booty, I don't know what is considered to be war booty.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Well, I think you've clarified the issue to a certain degree. What I'm suggesting is the case is that it was impossible for the border to prevent personal items being taken, because an individual could simply claim that the items belonged to them. But what the border could do, the border police and the military, is prevent weapons being brought over into Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. As I have said, weapons couldn't be taken over into Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'm just going to try and shortcut things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have P1081 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And I want to deal with the issue of Vaso Mijovic, what you know about him. Now, as we can see from this document, 15th of May, 1993, order: 1 there's an order that Mijovic resubordinate himself to the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. From what you observed, would you agree with me this, as a general proposition, from what you observed: The problem for the VRS at the time was that groups from within the VRS were prone to removing themselves from subordination and forming into semi-autonomous groups? Is that a general proposition you can agree with?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I could agree with that. That was a problem that we were aware of over there. People would organise themselves to defend their village. They didn't want to be under anyone's command, under the command of the army or the police. They quite simply defended their villages, and they didn't want to engage in the war. But some went. Others said, I'm the commander of the village, I'm defending my village. The other commander in another village would say, I'm defending my village. So it was a permanent problem. They couldn't organise themselves and place themselves under a single command. They persisted in just defending the territory of their own villages. So if that is your question, yes, various groups did exist under their own command, so to speak. There were such groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: So the suggestion here in this document that at one point Mijovic, who, from other evidence we've been discussing, was a member of the Red Berets, had at one point been a member of the Red Berets under the Bratunac Brigade, or Light Infantry Brigade, then he'd left, and then there was an order to resubordinate himself to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, which he then did, would be consistent with your understanding of how it worked with many of the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'm finding it a little hard to follow these compound questions. I'm not sure if it might be also the case with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let me simplify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This document suggests that Mijovic was subordinated to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, left, and then was ordered to return. That is consistent with what happened with many of the paramilitaries which formed in this area at that time. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't personally know anything about Vasilije Mijovic, but I'm familiar with that case over there. I know that they would be placed under one command and then they would leave. When another unit appeared, they would then join that unit. And then when that unit left, they would return to their previous units. I'm familiar with that phenomenon, so to speak, but I don't know about this particular individual. But I do know that such things did occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think, because of the time, what I'd like to do is, it's our submission that when one puts together the various documents which deal with the Red Berets in Bratunac with the documents relating to Vaso Mijovic, one can see precisely what happened and where Vaso Mijovic obtained his weapons and ammunition to be able to set himself up for -- as a semi-autonomous unit for approximately three to four months in 1993. And I would like to bar table, if possible, documents which fill in the gap, which exists at the moment in the documents which reflect -- which would reflect that story. If I may then apply to bar table D188, which was MNA'd, which is 30th of June, 1993, which is an order to prepare -- from the command of the Drina Corps to the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, for Mijovic to prepare his reconnaissance and sabotage unit to be under the command of Mijovic but to be subordinated, once again, to the Light Infantry Brigade. And, similarly, D186, MNA, which is 19th of April, 1993, which is a document which reflects the -- a similar attempt to resubordinate Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jordash, maybe you could make a submission later on or produce these documents later on, because -- when the witness is gone, because the witness told us that he did not know Mr. Miomir [as interpreted], so maybe that's the way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, I'll do that. May I just -- this is about Mijovic, but I want to ask about the principle, then I've finished. Could I have, please P1585, and it's B/C/S page 32. And it's from -- could this to be under seal, please. And it's from a personnel file relating to Mijovic. It's supposed to be Mijovic's DB file, according to the Prosecution. And it shows Mijovic being stopped at the border crossing at Mali Zvornik, and Mijovic getting out of his vehicle and asking if he could use the official telephone to call Sokolovic, minister of interior, and not being permitted to.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And I -- whilst it's not strictly necessary for you to look at it, I want you just to orientate yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps I can shortcut things. We are running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that nobody, as far as you were aware, had privileged status at the border to bring in weapons and ammunition from Serbia to Bosnia, or vice versa? And I include in that Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, at our border crossing at Skelani, no one could carry over weapons. While I was at the watch-tower, I am positive that during that period no one carried weapons and military equipment over the bridge. As I have said already, we were in contact with the police working there, and they, too, told me about it, saying that nobody could bring weapons. I agree with you that everyone enjoyed the same status, i.e., that no one was authorised to bring weapons across the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And you were never asked, were you, to look out for a particular Serbian MUP group and make sure that they could cross unhindered without -- with their weapons or ammunition or supplies such as that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You were never asked, were you, to allow any Serbian MUP unit to cross the border whilst carrying weapons and ammunition from Serbia into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one of asked any such thing of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I've got no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, would Your Honours excuse me? I have to leave. I've -- Mr. Martin will cover Mr. Stanisic's interests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Bakrac, do you have any questions in re-direct for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Certainly, Your Honour. I have additional questions. With your leave, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. And how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid I will barely finish by the end of this session. But I'll try to do everything in my power to conclude by 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask Ms. Harbour if she will have any other questions later, eventually? I don't know if you are able to answer now, but I'm putting the question to you nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... no questions arising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... no questions for now. I'm sorry, my microphone is not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard you. Thank you. Mr. Bakrac, if you could finish just a few minutes before the end of the hearing, that would really be great, because the Judges would also like to put a few questions to the witness. Would you be able to conclude before the end, a few minutes before the end? And I would also like to add -- or ask you, rather, if the next witness is already here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, although I'm not sure I'll succeed. I believe there are many important questions. And we have the next witness waiting. But I'm not certain I'll be able to cover all important questions I have. Well, I'll try. Perhaps we can start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, could we look at 2D525. My learned friend Ms. Harbour asked you about your marriage to a certain Aleksandra Bugarski. Can you tell us if you are still married? In other words, when did you marry Aleksandra Bugarski? And if you divorced her, when was that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am no longer married to Aleksandra Bugarski. We divorced in early 2000, I believe, after about a year and a half of being married.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, I have a decision here on the divorce of Mr. Franko Simatovic and Sanja Simatovic, maiden name Bugarski. As stated here, it was on the 11th of September, 1996. If we scroll up, we can see in the statement of reasons that the marriage was concluded on the 9th of July, 1995. It means that it lasted for just over a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript, I can see that the marriage was concluded on the 9th of July, 1995. And the divorce occurred in 1996. On the 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During this period, did you know Sanja Bugarski?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know your future wife Aleksandra Bugarski whom you married later on? Did you know her during this time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I've said, I only met her in 1998, when we also became married.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you became married, was Aleksandra Bugarski or members of her family, in any kind of contact with Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. They never mentioned being in contact with him. Sanja had divorced him, and for them it was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you ever, on that basis, the basis that you married the sister later on, did you ever meet with Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we next look at D456. Before that, could we have this judgement, which is on our 65 ter list be -- could we have it admitted in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Would you let us know what the provenance of this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: -- is?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, after a divorce, a copy of decisions kept by the partners, or the former partners, that's how it was provided to us by Franko Simatovic. Should you require any further explanation, we can receive appropriate documents from the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Harbour, I don't think that a divorce judgement can be challenged.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could we have an exhibit number, please. This will be MFI'd because the document hasn't been translated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise about having it translated. It any case, it will be done. Next could we please go to D456.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, my learned friend asked you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is under seal. This document is under seal, and I would kindly ask that it not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... document. As far as the divorce judgement is concerned, Registrar, your voice hasn't been recorded because your microphone was off. Could you repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter number 2D525 will be marked for identification as D871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned colleague is telling me that we do have a judgement of -- do have a translation of this judgement and that it has been uploaded into e-court. But not to waste any time on that, could we have D456, page 43 in B/C/S and 41 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, during your examination-in-chief you testified that you met three men at Petrova Gora. Once you returned to Serbia, they became members of the JATD. My learned friend showed you documents concerning Mico Petrakovic and Zoran Gulic. I would kindly ask you to look at this. This document comes from the personnel file of Dusan Momcilovic. It seems that it is a statement signed on has behalf in the presence of two witnesses. It is stated here that he was permanently employed with the RSK MUP and the Glina SUP between the 26th of June, 1991, and 5 August 1995. Could we please go to the bottom of the page so that you can see the signature on the left-hand side. Momcilovic, Dusan. Given that you say you met them at Petrova Gora between late April and late July 1995, does this fact, that Dusan Momcilovic was employed with the Glina SUP, correspond with what you heard from your superior or from them at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My superior told me that they were from the RSK MUP and that they were subordinated to the Pauk Command. That's what I needed to know, and that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have P399 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, I'll try to refresh your memory while we are waiting for the document. It is entitled: "Report on the Establishment of Units for Special Purposes, the Red Berets of the MUP of Serbia in Skelani." There was an abbreviation that was mentioned in this context and some discussion about the document itself. Could we look at the penultimate paragraph from the bottom. I'll read it out. It says: "Lately, the unit has spent some time in the area of the dry border in the area of Visegrad." My question is this: Visegrad and the dry border, is it in the Republic of Serbia or in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Visegrad is a town in Republika Srpska, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This document is dated the 15th of May, 1993. Which institutions existed in Visegrad at the time - those of Republika Srpska or the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'll keep reading: "They returned to the camp on the 14th of May..." So they returned, it seems, "... from Visegrad on the 14th of May, 1993, and refused to be placed under the command of the Skelani Independent Battalion, saying that only the RS MUP can command them, because that is what they had been told when they -- before they returned to Skelani." Do you allow for the possibility that this abbreviation, MUP RS, suggests the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my reading of the context would that it is the Republika Srpska MUP. As for the SBS abbreviation, it is very likely the Skelani Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, this document is dated the 15th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next move to P387 concerning this topic. It is dated the 17th of June, 1993, that is to say, a month following this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The SB Skelani Command issued this report on combat readiness. In item 1 - look at the last bullet point - it says: "I had a conversation with Mr. Markovic, Goran Markovic, deputy commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija-Bircani detachment of the special brigade of the MUP RS (a headache)." My question is this: The Sarajevo-Romanija-Bircani detachment of the special brigade of the MUP RS, this term, or geographical designation, "Sarajevo-Romanija-Bircani," does it tell you that it concerns the MUP of the Republic of Serbia or Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP of Republika Srpska. Sarajevo and Romanija are in Bosnia, and it's only logical that it is the Republika Srpska MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Then it continues: "At my insistence, Markovic reported that 57 military conscripts of the Skelani Battalion (Crvena Beretka) were formed into a special platoon that joined the Srb detachment of the Misa Pelemis company." Did you ever here, of the Sarajevo-Romanija-Bircani of the special brigade of the MUP of Republika Srpska, that there was certain Misa Pelemis and his company as part of that formation?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unaware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you are not aware of Misa Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, your question was whether I had ever heard of him, and my answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about later when you became member of the JATD? You did not encounter such a person in the JATD? Did you hear your colleagues mention a certain Misa Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I hear of that first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. I'll go back to P399; the first paragraph. The document titled: "Formation of the Red Berets Special-Purposes Unit of the MUP in Skelani." Well, it says the following: "The Red Berets unit was established on the 8th of June, 1992. It had 20 military conscripts and was under the command of three instructors who trained the soldiers. The unit continued to grow, and there are 50 soldiers in the camp in the school now. "Since September 1992, only persons who did not complete their military service have been sent to the Red Berets unit in order to - text missing - through basic military training." I read out this portion. Please bear it in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I wish to go to P2104 next. It is dated the 3rd of August, 1992. There was some mention that in June 1992 a training camp was established at the school facility with three instructors.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at this document sent by Drago Nikolic, desk clerk or desk officer, who sent it to the commander of the East Bosnia Corps. The title is: "Operations by Red Berets Units in the Ranks of the Army of the SRBH." The first paragraph reads: "At the beginning of June 1992" -- in the previous document, we saw that the unit was establish on the 8th of June. "At the beginning of June 1992, a training camp was organised in the Serbian municipality of Skelani for members of the Serbian army from a few municipalities in the Birac region. The camp was managed by a certain Pupovac, from Captain Dragan's group, who hails from the Knin Krajina. All those attending the training in the camp received food from the army and they have enhanced nutrition. Apart from exercises to improve their physical condition and endures, they have only had a few sessions of firing practice and a couple of tactical exercises. After completion of the training of the first group of camp attendees, the camp continued its activity and the group that had completed --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: the groups that had completed training.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: "... returned to their home municipalities." Mr. Plahuta, did you know that in the school in Skelani there was a training camp for certain people?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were aware of that camp in late 1992, when I transferred to the watch-tower. We were informed that there was a training camp accommodating members from Republika Srpska. We needed to know about them so that in case of significant movements we should not be alarmed or resort to weapons, since the school was visible from our side. It was some two kilometres away from the bridge in Skelani. We could see it. It was in Bosnia. And we knew there was a training camp in the school training their police or army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I've been very hesitant to object just because of the time, but I do want to remind everyone that this is re-direct and there have been some very leading questions, as well as in this instance, putting a number of documents to the witness before asking him about the issue, whereas usually the practice is the reverse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right. You are quite right. Mr. Bakrac, I know that you're pressed for time, that you're trying to do your best, but please try not to put any leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's the reason. But if you have a look at the summary for this witness -- well, perhaps I omitted to mention this in my direct examination, but this is reaction to the cross-examination, but if you have a look at the summary for this witness, it says that this witness knows that in the Bajina Basta area near Skelani there were refugees from Krajina. And also that there was training camp for the police of Republika Srpska which was located in the Skelani school where there was also a playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Plahuta, my question is: Are you sure that that centre for training in the school was used for the police or for the army?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a centre for the police from Republika Srpska. That was the centre located in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the summary you said that you knew that there were some refugees there. Do you know where those refugees were from, and do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their names, but I do know that the refugees were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I unfortunately object to this line of questioning because the summary is not in evidence. If you'd like to elicit this evidence from the witness, that would be another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned colleague tried, in the course of her cross-examination, to link up a group of the Red Berets from Skelani with the DB in Serbia with our client, Simatovic. I'm now trying to use these documents to establish what this witness knows about this issue, and I'm also showing that in his summary he had information about some individuals who stayed in the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. But we don't have the summary of his statement, so the question you are putting to him at the moment are closed questions. So please pay more attention to the way in which you put your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honours. I thought that in the request to add this witness there was also a summary included. But I do apologise. I'll bear this in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, let's now have a look at exhibit -- before we have look at the exhibit, my question, Mr. Plahuta, is as follows: Along the border along the Drina in Bajina Basta was there a lorry of some kind with an antenna that moved along with the border?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean with antenna for electronic surveillance? Yes. A lorry for electronic surveillance did appear from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Plahuta, let's please have a look at Exhibit 3119 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I apologise, Your Honours. Exhibit P3118.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, here mention was made of the Udar operation in 1993, and my learned colleague showed you an analysis of the combat conducted under the code-name Udar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's please have a look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to ask you the following: It says in order to carry out Operation Udar certain forces should be engaged. Under (a), from the corps; and under (b), from outside the corps. Please have a look at this document and tell me whether you can see the Red Beret unit from the Serbian MUP mentioned anywhere here?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see anything here. I can't see that here, but I don't know whether I have the right document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page in the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Here we can see the Vlasenica military platoon. It's outside the corps formation. The VRS Sabotage Detachment. The Main Staff VRS sabotage detachment. And do you see the Red Berets from Skelani anywhere here?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know who was present? We can see that the combat is under the command of Lieutenant Dragomir Milosevic in this operation order. Do you know which unit he was a member of and which army?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. As I said, before this Operation Udar, I similarly couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plahuta. Mr. Plahuta, can you tell me, my learned colleague asked you about your personnel file and asked you about the Official Note according to which you were suspected of smoking grass and so on and so forth. Did anyone ever see you acting in this way or --

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, so that you don't have to go on, I can quite simply say that I have never smoked grass. No one ever saw me doing that. No one every found any opiates of any kind on me. I never used any such opiates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If this had been found on you, given the code that the unit abides by and given the regulations, would disciplinary procedures have been initiated against you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would have been removed from the unit forthwith.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you assumed that this report was made because you had a scarf with the American flag on it and you wore an earring. Did you dress in that way when you were on duty in the unit, or did you dress in that way when you went to town?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was on duty I would never dress like that. When I was on duty, I was always dressed in accordance with the regulations. But what I wore in my free time is the manner in which I went to town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Given the allegations made by certain individuals with regard to you, were any proceedings initiated against you, and were you held to account because of the criticisms levelled at you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never head to account for anything of that kind. You can check this. I was never punished, although it says so. I was never punished, and nothing was ever deducted from my salary as a form of punishment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bakrac, it is 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see that, Your Honour. I'm looking at two documents. My colleague Jordash examined the witness with regard to those documents. Both were P documents. I think that we can deal with them in the analysis. I don't think we need the witness for this, so I will leave these two documents out for the moment. And thank you for the time you granted me. That's all I had for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do you wish to ask any further questions or not? That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were shown a document, D860, which then had a bad translation - but a better translation has been prepared meanwhile, Mr. Bakrac - dealing with a request from the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade to the command of the 72nd Special Brigade to provide red berets. Do you remember that document? Otherwise perhaps it could be shown. D860.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It -- it mentions the Podrinje detachment, numbering 350 soldiers. Do you know whether the Podrinje detachment -- do you know anything about the Podrinje detachment?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, no. I don't know anything about them. They were downstream from where we were located. Bratunac is 50 or 60 kilometres from Bajina Basta, and Zvornik is almost 100 kilometres from Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of them. I never actually had contact with them, but I did hear about the existence of such a unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a Podrinje detachment being called the Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know which unit went by that name. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then take it that you're unfamiliar with the -- where the soldiers came from which were serving in the Podrinje detachment?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no further questions apparently, unless the questions of the Bench have triggered any. This concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for answering all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you, too, for the warm welcome I received in your country and for the fact that I was able to assist both parties in these proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn for the day. And we will resume on -- let me have a look. I think it would be the 22nd of May, at 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom, II. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of May, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
